title: A put-back erase says no reason: the iPhone shows an empty one, the web a generic failure
evidence: Found at the checkpoint 3 look-back of S57. When the cloud definitely refused the erase write and the device copy did not land, eraseSession puts the pre-erase copy back and answers { success: false } with no error string (packages/health-core/src/record-session-erase.ts:163-166; the other failure path at :167 passes the message). iPhone: DataEraser.swift:190-197 reads answer?.error ?? "", so after the chat step (chatWritten or cloudChatErased) EraseText.failed('', ...) builds "Your record was not erased.  Your chat history was deleted." with an empty reason and a doubled space (ios/HealthRoadmap/MyData/EraseText.swift:79-85); with no chat step it calls EraseText.refusal(nil, ...), which says the provider could not be reached (EraseText.swift:73-76), also not what happened. The engine's answer is the same on every build. Web: useErase.ts:132 falls back to ERASE_FAILED ('Failed to delete data. Please try again.', widget-src/src/lib/erase-copy.ts:79), as the comment at useErase.ts:129 states. Proposal: the engine returns a refusal string on the put-back (for example that the cloud refused the erase and nothing was erased), which both clients then show. New user-facing words, so Brad's. US-11 AC3b, AC7
